scope: 32 frozen before/after engine scenarios from real-game positions and constructed controls, plus separately tested colour-reflected controls. Reused development data, not new games, holdout validation or general accuracy. Engine lines are frozen depth-16 evidence, not fresh searches in this report.

cases.name: The real Kf1 best defence does not cause the existing mate
cases.explanation: Ncd4 is a quiet mating preparation. All 16 legal White replies allow forced mate within two more moves; for example, Rb1 Ne3+ Kg1 Rxg2#. Kf1 is also the analysed best move. The same position and tactical danger remain after either choice. This threat alone does not explain the difference between the two moves.

cases.name: The real Bh3 mistake misses Qxc6+'s mate, not just the knight
cases.explanation: The better move had this tactic: Qxc6+ starts a forced mating attack. Every legal defence permits mate within 3 moves; one verified line is Qxc6+ Qd7 Qxa8+ Qc8 Qxc8#. The exact continuation depends on the defence.

cases.name: Pushed too early instead of removing the promotion-path defender (MJZcU)
cases.explanation: The better move had this tactic: Rxe4 removes the knight on e4, which controlled d2. The passed pawns on c3 and d4 can advance. All 21 legal replies permit a verified local material gain or mate, including recaptures and checking defences; one line is Rxe4 fxe4 c2 Rd7+ Ke6 Rc7 d3 a3 d2 Rc6+ Ke5 Rc5+ Kd4 Rd5+ Ke3 Rxd2 c1=Q.

cases.name: Left the queen behind the discovered checking capture
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Bxh7+ vacates e4, uncovering the rook on e1 against the queen on e8. The moving bishop gives check, so the opponent cannot simply ignore the exposed attack. Every legal reply concedes material. Captures and interpositions are included in this check. g6 makes the immediate reply Bxh7+ illegal.

cases.name: A different reply wins the same queen after the better move
cases.explanation: Re8+ exploits the queen on f8, pinned to the king on h8 by the rook on e8. No legal reply avoids material loss in the immediate exchange. Even after Kg7, Rf5+ still forces at least the same net material gain on the queen on f8. The better move changes the continuation, not the existence of that material loss. This threat alone does not explain the difference between the two moves.

cases.name: Ignored double-check mate instead of making a king escape
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Bb5# vacates e2, uncovering the rook on e1 against the king on e8. Both pieces give check. There is no legal defence: checkmate. Rg8+ makes the immediate reply Bb5# illegal.

cases.name: Failed to unpin the knight
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: d6 exploits the knight on e7, pinned to the king on e8 by the rook on e1. Every non-checking reply allows material loss. Checking replies remain, so the capture is a threat, not a guaranteed immediate win. After Kd7, Kxd6 answers d6; a profitable immediate follow-up capture of the knight on e7 is no longer forced.

cases.name: Allowed a king-queen skewer instead of preserving the queen
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Bd3+ skewers the king on f5 and the queen on h7. No legal reply saves the rear target without conceding material. After Kf4, Qxd3 answers Bd3; a profitable immediate follow-up capture of the queen on h7 is no longer forced.

cases.name: Allowed checking defender removal and lost the queen
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: gxf6+ removes the knight on f6 that defended the queen on d5, with check. Every legal reply allows a profitable capture of that target. Qxd1+ makes the immediate reply gxf6+ illegal. You also missed a tactical opportunity (Hanging Piece): Qxd1+ wins the loose rook on d1.

cases.explanation: The better move had this tactic: Qh2 is a quiet mating preparation. All 4 legal Black replies allow forced mate within two more moves; for example, h5 Kxg6 h4 Qb8#. Your move also allowed an opponent tactic (Hanging Piece): gxh5 wins the loose queen on h5. Qh2 makes the immediate reply gxh5 illegal.

cases.name: Missed the quiet rook preparation for mate or a queen skewer

cases.name: Recaptured the rook before taking the queen with check
cases.explanation: The better move had this tactic: Bxd2+ takes the queen with check before Rxh8. Every legal answer to the check preserves extra material through the deferred capture or the piece taking the checker. Playing Rxh8 first allows Qxg5, preventing an immediate profitable capture of that queen. The move order matters, not just the two captures.

cases.name: b6 permits the f7 fork
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Nxf7 forks the queen on d8 and rook on h8. The bishop on c4 protects f7, so the king cannot capture the knight. The line continues with Nxd8, winning the queen. After O-O, Nxf7 no longer has two profitable fork targets.

cases.name: The real Ke8 mistake allows a mating attack with quiet preparation

Every legal defence permits mate within 7 moves; one verified line is f7+ Ke7 fxg8=B g5 Bc4 g4 Qf7+ Kd6 Ne4+ Kc6 Qd5+ Kb6 Qb5#. The exact continuation depends on the defence. Kxf6 makes the immediate reply f7+ illegal.

cases.name: The real Rc5 mistake permits a checking fork preparation
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Rb1+ prepares a checking fork. After Kf2, Nd3+ forks the king on f2 and rook on c5. Blocking with Rc1 instead allows Rxc1+, winning the blocking piece. All 2 legal replies allow a verified gain; captures, interpositions and legal recaptures are included. The fork belongs to the next move, not this board position. After Ra5, Kf2 answers Rb1+ without permitting a checking fork or capture of the rook on a5 on the next move. This prevents this immediate preparation, not every possible later attack.

cases.name: The real g6 mistake permits Nd7's double threat
cases.explanation: Your move allowed this tactic: Nd7 attacks the rook on b6 and threatens Nf6+, a checking fork of the queen on h5 and king on g8. After Kg7, Nxb6 wins material; after Rc6, Nf6+ uses the fork instead. All 35 legal replies allow a verified material gain, including captures and counterchecks. This is a double threat now; the fork occurs on the next move only if that branch is played. After Bg6, Rbxa6 answers Nd7 with a countercapture. Including that captured material and legal recaptures, the immediate threats cannot force a pawn's worth of material gain. The immediate checks have concrete answers: Nf6+ gxf6. This prevents this local winning double threat, not every possible later combination or positional loss.

cases.name: The real Re2 mistake allows a forcing checking attack

The continuation depends on the defence; later pins and forks belong to their actual positions, not the opening check. After Kc1, Qf1 is not check and Rxf1 captures the attacking queen on f1. Legal immediate replies, recaptures and one countercheck cannot erase the local material gain. This refutes this checking sequence, not every possible later attack.

cases.explanation: The better move had this tactic: Ne5 vacates d7, uncovering the rook on d8 against the knight on d4. The knight on e5 also attacks the queen on d3 and the bishop on c4. The shared defence cannot save all these targets: after Qc3, Qxc3 removes the defender. Every legal reply permits a local material gain, including the defender exchange and up to two checking counterattacks; recaptures and exposed attacking pieces are included.
